headline: Subscriber losses pressure revenue as buybacks lift EPS
summary_short: Charter's Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 1.7% y/y to $13.5 billion as Internet and video customer losses outweighed mobile growth, while heavy share buybacks lifted diluted EPS 16.1% to $10.66 even as Adjusted EBITDA declined 4.3%.
summary_long: Revenue declined 1.7% y/y to $13.5 billion, driven by lower residential video and Internet revenue (higher costs allocated to streaming apps within video, and a shrinking Internet base), partly offset by 18.9% mobile service revenue growth. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.3% to $5.4 billion as revenue declined while operating costs held flat; income from operations fell 6.6% to $3.1 billion. Net income was roughly flat at $1.3 billion, helped by a gain on debt extinguishment. Diluted EPS rose 16.1% to $10.66 on a roughly 14% cut in diluted share count from buybacks ($838 million of stock repurchased). Free cash flow fell to $969 million on a working-capital swing. Charter reiterated full-year 2026 capex of approximately $11.4 billion, excluding Cox-transaction impacts.

drivers.explanation: Lower residential video and Internet revenue (partly from higher streaming-app costs netted within video revenue, plus fewer Internet/video customers) outweighed growth in mobile service and advertising revenue.
Follows the same pattern management cited for Adjusted EBITDA: revenue declined 1.7% while total operating costs and expenses stayed roughly flat year-over-year.
Lower Adjusted EBITDA was offset by a gain on extinguishment of debt tied to open-market debt repurchases in the quarter.
Company attributed the per-share earnings increase to a double-digit year-over-year cut in weighted-average shares outstanding from continued buybacks.
Total debt held roughly flat as $4.4 billion of new quarterly long-term borrowings was largely offset by $4.6 billion of repayments, per the cash-flow statement.
Management pointed to the pending Cox Communications transaction, continued network evolution, and a converged connectivity strategy as priorities amid competitive pressure across all product lines.
